The final match of the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]]—the 23rd edition of the [[FIFA]] competition for men's national [[Association football|soccer]] teams—was played at [[MetLife Stadium]] in [[East Rutherford, New Jersey]], part of the [[New York metropolitan area]], on July 19, 2026. It was contested by [[Spain national football team|Spain]] and the then defending champion [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]].    

The tournament was contested by hosts [[Canada men's national soccer team|Canada]], [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]], and the [[United States men's national soccer team|United States]], along with 45 other teams who emerged from [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification|the qualification phase]], which was organized by the six [[List of football federations#Continental|FIFA confederations]]. The 48 teams competed in a group stage, from which 32 teams qualified for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup knockout stage|knockout stage]]. En route to the final, Spain finished first in [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group H|Group H]] with two wins and a draw, before defeating [[Austria national football team|Austria]] in the round of 32, [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]] in the round of 16, [[Belgium national football team|Belgium]] in the quarterfinal, and [[France national football team|France]] in the semifinal. Argentina finished first in [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group J|Group J]] with three wins, after which it defeated [[Cape Verde national football team|Cape Verde]] in the round of 32, [[Egypt national football team|Egypt]] in the round of 16, [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland]] in the quarterfinal, and [[England national football team|England]] in the semifinal. The final took place in front of 80,663 spectators, and was [[Referee (association football)|refereed]] by [[Slavko Vinčić]] of Slovenia. 

Spain dominated possession and created numerous goal-scoring opportunities throughout the match, with Argentina goalkeeper [[Emiliano Martínez]] repeatedly denying its offensive efforts. Argentina, reduced to ten players after [[Enzo Fernández]] was [[Fouls and misconduct (association football)#Red card (dismissal)|sent off]] in the second half, failed to register a single shot in [[Glossary of association football terms#Regulation time|regulation time]], a first for a World Cup final. The goalless deadlock carried into [[Overtime (sports)|extra time]], during which [[Ferran Torres]] scored from a [[Nico Williams]] header to secure a 1–0 victory for Spain. With a few minutes left, Argentina missed multiple opportunities to equalize the score. After the match, a brawl broke out between the two teams. 

Spain's win earned the country its [[List of FIFA World Cup finals|second World Cup title]] and its first since [[2010 FIFA World Cup final|2010]]. Torres was named the [[man of the match]], and Emiliano Martínez's 11 saves set a record for the most saves by a goalkeeper in a World Cup final. The match was the first ever World Cup final to include a [[2026 FIFA World Cup final halftime show|halftime show]], which caused the full halftime break to last over 27 minutes, against [[International Football Association Board]] (IFAB) protocol. Spain became the first country to simultaneously hold the men's and women's World Cup titles, having won the [[FIFA Women's World Cup]] in [[2023 FIFA Women's World Cup|2023]].

==Background==
[[File:P20260719DT-1368 President Donald J. Trump and First Lady Melania Trump attend the FIFA World Cup Final.jpg|thumb|The ''Trionda Final'' ball used in the final.]]The [[2026 FIFA World Cup]] was the 23rd edition of the [[FIFA World Cup|World Cup]], [[FIFA]]'s [[association football|soccer]] competition for men's national teams, held in Canada, Mexico and the United States between June 11 and July 19, 2026.<ref name="Britanica">{{Cite encyclopedia |url-status=live|title=World Cup: History & Winners|last1=Tikkanen|first1=Amy|last2=Augustyn|first2=Adam|last3=Levy|first3=Michael|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210828023709/https://www.britannica.com/sports/World-Cup-football|archive-date=28 August 2021|last4=Ray|first4=Michael|last5=Luebering|first5=J. E.|last6=Lotha|first6=Gloria|last7=Young|first7=Grace|last8=Shepherd|first8=Melinda C.|last9=Sinha|first9=Surabhi|last10=Rodriguez|first10=Emily|encyclopedia=[[Encyclopædia Britannica]]|date=19 August 2021|access-date=22 September 2021|url=https://www.britannica.com/sports/World-Cup-football}}</ref><ref name="Reuters">{{cite news |title=FIFA World Cup 2026: Fixtures, results, group standings & bracket |url=https://www.reuters.com/graphics/SOCCER-WORLDCUP/mopaoglqkpa/ |work=[[Reuters]] |accessdate=July 17, 2026 |archive-date=July 18, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260718151218/https://www.reuters.com/graphics/SOCCER-WORLDCUP/mopaoglqkpa/ |url-status=live}}</ref> The tournament featured 48 teams for the first time, up from 32 in the [[2022 FIFA World Cup|2022 World Cup]].<ref name="Anderson-2025" /> The national teams of [[Canada men's national soccer team|Canada]], [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]] and the [[United States men's national soccer team|United States]] qualified automatically for the tournament as hosts, while 206 teams competed for the remaining 45 slots through [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification|qualifying rounds]] organized by the six [[List of football federations#Continental|FIFA confederations]] and held between September 2023 and March 2026.<ref name="Anderson-2025">{{cite news |last=Anderson |first=Jason |date=October 8, 2025 |title=What teams are qualified for 2026 World Cup? Full list, latest updates |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/worldcup/2025/10/08/world-cup-2026-qualified-teams-soccer/86584914007/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251011215832/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/worldcup/2025/10/08/world-cup-2026-qualified-teams-soccer/86584914007/ |archive-date=October 11, 2025 |accessdate=July 17, 2026 |work=[[USA Today]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=September 3, 2025 |title=FIFA World Cup 2026 qualifying: All you need to know |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/road-to-world-cup-26-qualifiers-usa-canada-mexico |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250321160145/https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/road-to-world-cup-26-qualifiers-usa-canada-mexico/ |archive-date=March 21, 2025 |accessdate=July 17, 2026 |publisher=[[FIFA]]}}</ref> In the tournament, the teams were divided into twelve groups of four, with each team playing every other team once in a [[Round-robin tournament|round-robin]] format. The top two teams from each group, along with the top eight third-place teams, advanced to the [[2026 FIFA World Cup knockout stage|knockout stage]].<ref>{{cite news|last=McKessy|first=Jack|date=June 25, 2026|title=How does the World Cup work? Rules, everything to know about 2026 tournament|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/worldcup/2026/06/25/world-cup-2026-explained-what-to-know/90696906007/|work=USA Today|accessdate=July 17, 2026|archive-date=July 18, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260718054101/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/worldcup/2026/06/25/world-cup-2026-explained-what-to-know/90696906007/|url-status=live}}</ref>   

[[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] had won the previous World Cup in Qatar in [[2022 FIFA World Cup|2022]], defeating [[France national football team|France]] in a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] in the [[2022 FIFA World Cup final|final]] after the match finished 3–3 after extra time. Argentina had previously won the World Cup in [[1978 FIFA World Cup|1978]] and [[1986 FIFA World Cup|1986]], and finished as runners-up in [[1930 FIFA World Cup|1930]], [[1990 FIFA World Cup|1990]], and [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Reineking |first=Jim |date=July 15, 2026 |title=How many World Cups has Argentina won? History beckons for Lionel Messi |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/worldcup/2026/07/15/argentina-world-cup-wins-all-time-messi/90923499007/ |work=USA Today |accessdate=July 17, 2026 |archive-date=July 16, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260716125741/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/worldcup/2026/07/15/argentina-world-cup-wins-all-time-messi/90923499007/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Argentina manager [[Lionel Scaloni]] was attempting to become the second manager to win multiple World Cup titles, after [[Vittorio Pozzo]] of Italy in [[1934 FIFA World Cup|1934]] and [[1938 FIFA World Cup|1938]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/spain-argentina-final-report-highlights|title=Torres puts Spain on top of the world|publisher=FIFA|date=19 July 2026}}</ref> Spain had won the World Cup once before in [[2010 FIFA World Cup|2010]], defeating [[Netherlands national football team|the Netherlands]] in the [[2010 FIFA World Cup final|final]] in [[Johannesburg]], South Africa.<ref name="Britanica" /> Heading into the 2026 final, Spain was tied with [[Italy national football team|Italy]] for the [[List of world association football records#Longest streaks|longest undefeated streak]] in the history of men's international soccer, with 37 matches.<ref>{{cite news |last=Gitto |first=Andrew |date=July 16, 2026 |title=Spain unbeaten streak record: Inside La Roja's record-tying 37-match run without a loss since 2024 |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/soccer/news/spain-unbeaten-streak-record-inside-record-37-match-2024/726212e1dda1dced7763d54f |work=[[The Sporting News]] |accessdate=July 17, 2026 |archive-date=July 15, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260715111258/https://www.sportingnews.com/us/soccer/news/spain-unbeaten-streak-record-inside-record-37-match-2024/726212e1dda1dced7763d54f |url-status=live }}</ref>

Spain and Argentina had played each other fourteen times since 1952, with each team winning six matches. They had played one World Cup match before, in the group stage of the [[1966 FIFA World Cup|1966 tournament]], with Argentina winning 2–1. Their most recent meeting before the 2026 World Cup was a [[Exhibition game|friendly]] match in [[Madrid]] on March 27, 2018, which Spain won 6–1.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/spain/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Argentina/ |title=Spain national football team: record v Argentina |work=11v11.com |publisher=[[Association of Football Statisticians]] |accessdate=July 14, 2026 |archive-date=July 16, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260716015108/https://www.11v11.com/teams/spain/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Argentina/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Spain and Argentina, respective winners of the [[UEFA European Championship]] and [[Copa América]] in 2024,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Morse |first=Ben |date=July 14, 2024 |title=Spain wins Euro 2024, defeating England 2-1 in a dramatic final to claim record fourth European Championship |url=https://www.cnn.com/2024/07/14/sport/spain-england-euro-2024-final-spt-intl |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240715120714/https://www.cnn.com/2024/07/14/sport/spain-england-euro-2024-final-spt-intl/ |archive-date=July 15, 2024 |access-date=July 28, 2026 |website=[[CNN]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=July 15, 2024 |title=Argentina edge Colombia to win record 16th Copa América title |url=https://abcnews.com/Sports/argentina-edge-colombia-win-record-16th-copa-amrica/story?id=111943591 |work=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]] |agency=ESPN News Services |accessdate=July 17, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260727155958/https://abcnews.com/Sports/argentina-edge-colombia-win-record-16th-copa-amrica/story?id=111943591|archive-date=July 27, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> were scheduled to contest the 2026 Finalissima in Qatar in March 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 18, 2024 |title=When is the 2025 Finalissima? |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/2025-finalissima-120000471.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250522174938/https://sports.yahoo.com/2025-finalissima-120000471.html |archive-date=May 22, 2025 |access-date=July 28, 2026 |website=[[Yahoo Sports]] |agency=[[90min]]}}</ref> However, the match was cancelled due to regional security concerns surrounding the [[2026 Iran war|Iran war]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Kallas |first=Fernando |date=July 17, 2026 |title=Messi's Argentina face Spain's cool machine in World Cup final rich with personal twists |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/messis-argentina-face-spains-cool-machine-world-cup-final-rich-with-personal-2026-07-17/ |work=Reuters |accessdate=July 17, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260727160254/https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/messis-argentina-face-spains-cool-machine-world-cup-final-rich-with-personal-2026-07-17/|archive-date=July 27, 2026|url-status=live|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=March 15, 2026 |title=Argentina vs. Spain Finalissima in Qatar called off after widening of Middle East war |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/spain-argentina-qatar-soccer-finalissima-cancelled-9.7129565 |work=[[CBC Sports]] |agency=[[Thomson Reuters]] |accessdate=July 17, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260316015858/https://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/spain-argentina-qatar-soccer-finalissima-cancelled-9.7129565|archive-date=March 16, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref>  

The 2026 final was the first World Cup final to feature two reigning continental champions, who were the two top-ranked teams in the [[FIFA World Ranking]].<ref name="Athletic-Everything">{{cite news |last1=Bushnell |first1=Henry |last2=Carey |first2=Mark |last3=Anzidei |first3=Melanie |last4=Stanton |first4=John |display-authors=etal |date=July 17, 2026 |title=World Cup final 2026: Everything you need to know |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7446983/2026/07/17/world-cup-final-everything-you-need-to-know/ |work=[[The Athletic]] |url-access=subscription |accessdate=July 17, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260718030648/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7446983/2026/07/17/world-cup-final-everything-you-need-to-know/|archive-date=July 18, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> It was also the second time that two [[Spanish language|Spanish]]-speaking countries competed against each other, after [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay]] and Argentina contested the inaugural [[1930 FIFA World Cup final|1930 final]]. With Spain and Argentina co-hosting the next World Cup in [[2030 FIFA World Cup|2030]], it meant the winner of this final would be the first-ever team to host a World Cup as the defending champion.{{efn|Attributed to multiple references:<ref>{{cite news |last=Rey |first=Débora |date=July 17, 2026 |title=Argentines and Spaniards face divided loyalties ahead of Spain-Argentina World Cup final |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2026/07/17/argentina-spain-brotherhood/ |work=[[Orlando Sentinel]] |agency=Associated Press |accessdate=July 17, 2026 |archive-date=July 18, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260718021250/https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2026/07/17/argentina-spain-brotherhood/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hodge |first=Mark |date=July 17, 2026 |title=From The Sports Desk: A blockbuster World Cup Final |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/sports/soccer/sports-newsletter-world-cup-final-rcna587988 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260717214915/https://www.nbcnews.com/sports/soccer/sports-newsletter-world-cup-final-rcna587988 |archive-date=July 17, 2026 |access-date=July 20, 2026 |publisher=[[NBC News]] }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Goldstein |first=Steven Louis |date=July 19, 2026 |title=World Cup final 2026: What U.S. viewers need to know to watch Spain vs. Argentina |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7452672/2026/07/19/world-cup-final-spain-argentina-yamal-messi-tv/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260720005623/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7452672/2026/07/19/world-cup-final-spain-argentina-yamal-messi-tv/ |archive-date=July 20, 2026 |access-date=July 20, 2026 |work=[[The Athletic]]|issn=0362-4331}}</ref>}} The official match ball used in the semifinals, match for third place, and the final, was a variation of the [[Adidas Trionda]] called the ''Trionda Final''. It has the same technical specifications as the Adidas Trionda, but has a gold, white, and black design that resembles the [[FIFA World Cup Trophy]].<ref>{{cite press release |date=July 6, 2026 |title=Final four World Cup 2026 matches to be played with Trionda Final Official Match Ball |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/trionda-final-official-match-ball-final-four-matches |publisher=[[FIFA]] |accessdate=July 17, 2026 |archive-date=July 12, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260712091130/https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/trionda-final-official-match-ball-final-four-matches |url-status=live }}</ref>

considered an early frontrunner to host the final due to its proximity to New York City and experience hosting major sporting events.{{Efn|Attributed to multiple references:<ref>{{cite news In 2021, a joint bid by New York and New Jersey was submitted for MetLife Stadium to host multiple matches during the 2026 World Cup.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 16, 2022 |title=New York / New Jersey |url-status=live }}</ref>''<ref name="Dominski-2024" />

The [[New Jersey Sports and Exposition Authority]] (NJSEA), which oversees MetLife Stadium, approved a $15.9 million contract to expand the stadium in June 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sobko |first=Katie |last2=Anzidei |first2=Melanie |date=June 23, 2023 |title=This is what the NJSEA will spend to renovate MetLife Stadium for FIFA World Cup Soccer |url=https://www.northjersey.com/story/sports/soccer/2023/06/23/fifa-world-cup-2026-metlife-stadium-cost-renovation-location/70347092007/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230703163919/https://eu.northjersey.com/story/sports/soccer/2023/06/23/fifa-world-cup-2026-metlife-stadium-cost-renovation-location/70347092007/ |archive-date=July 3, 2023 |access-date=July 22, 2026 |website=[[North Jersey Media Group]] |language=en-US |url-status=live |url-access=subscription}}</ref> In preparation for the World Cup, the stadium's field was widened to meet FIFA's size requirements,<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 23, 2024 |title=World Cup final coming in 2026. Here's the latest on N.J.'s big plans to be ready for it. |url=https://www.nj.com/news/2024/03/world-cup-finals-coming-in-2026-heres-the-latest-on-njs-big-plans-to-be-ready-for-it.html |url-status=live |access-date=July 28, 2026 |website=[[NJ.com]] |language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240323184445/https://www.nj.com/news/2024/03/world-cup-finals-coming-in-2026-heres-the-latest-on-njs-big-plans-to-be-ready-for-it.html|archive-date=March 23, 2024|last=Higgs|first=Larry|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and [[Bermuda grass]] was temporarily laid over the field's [[artificial turf]] for the World Cup.<ref>{{cite news |last=Bushnell |first=Henry |date=February 3, 2026 |title=How NFL stadiums are transforming for the 2026 World Cup |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7007467/2026/02/03/2026-world-cup-nfl-stadiums/ |work=The Athletic |url-access=subscription |accessdate=July 17, 2026 |archive-date=February 3, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260203123014/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7007467/2026/02/03/2026-world-cup-nfl-stadiums/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Anzidei |first=Melanie |date=May 8, 2026 |title=Installing the World Cup final pitch: 27 trucks, a 12-hour journey and 10-hour shifts |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7263429/2026/05/08/new-york-new-jersey-world-cup-stadium-grass-turf-installation/ |work=The Athletic |url-access=subscription |access-date=July 5, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260509072506/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7263429/2026/05/08/new-york-new-jersey-world-cup-stadium-grass-turf-installation/|archive-date=May 9, 2026}}</ref> The field was later criticized by players, including [[Vinícius Júnior]] and [[Adrien Rabiot]], both of whom said it was too dry. Worn patches on the pitch were noted by the media.<ref>{{cite news |last=Battison |first=Paul |date=June 17, 2026 |title=Rabiot raises concerns about MetLife Stadium pitch |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cevld1m8nxno |work=BBC Sport |accessdate=July 5, 2026 |archive-date=July 16, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260716201524/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cevld1m8nxno |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Anzidei |first=Melanie |date=June 21, 2026 |title=Is MetLife Stadium's pitch fit to host the World Cup final? Players and coaches have concerns |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7377642/2026/06/21/metlife-pitch-world-cup-final-fifa/ |work=The Athletic |url-access=subscription |access-date=July 5, 2026 |archive-date=July 13, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260713160914/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7377642/2026/06/21/metlife-pitch-world-cup-final-fifa/ |url-status=live}}</ref> The [[Meadowlands Rail Line]] and a $35 million bus line, referred to as the [[Bus rapid transit in New Jersey#Secaucus to Meadowlands Transitway|Secaucus-Meadowlands Transitway]], were used to transport attendees from the nearest transit hub at [[Secaucus Junction]].{{Efn|Attributed to multiple references:<ref>{{cite news |last=Nessen |first=Stephen |date=February 6, 2024 |title=Is NJ Transit up for hosting the World Cup in 2026? Commuters are skeptical. |url=https://gothamist.com/news/nj-transit-world-cup-train-delays-2014-super-bowl |accessdate=February 13, 2024 |work=[[Gothamist]] |archive-date=October 21, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251021105344/https://gothamist.com/news/nj-transit-world-cup-train-delays-2014-super-bowl |url-status=live |url-access=registration}}</ref><ref name="AP-Stadium22">{{cite news |last=Blum |first=Ronald |date=February 4, 2024 |title=2026 World Cup final will be played at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/soccer/2024/02/04/2026-world-cup-schedule/1c65f7a0-c3a0-11ee-bbc9-9b5ca9b20779_story.html |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |agency=Associated Press |accessdate=February 4, 2024|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Higgs |first=Larry |date=February 6, 2024 |title=NJ Transit will operate 'on steroids' during the World Cup, Murphy says. Here's the plan. |url=https://www.nj.com/news/2024/02/nj-transit-will-operate-on-steroids-during-the-world-cup-murphy-says-heres-the-plan.html |work=[[The Star-Ledger]]|url-access=subscription |accessdate=February 13, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240207002134/https://www.nj.com/news/2024/02/nj-transit-will-operate-on-steroids-during-the-world-cup-murphy-says-heres-the-plan.html|archive-date=February 7, 2024}}</ref>}} In April 2026, [[NJ Transit]], which operates the Meadowlands Rail Line, announced that $150 tickets, higher than the usual $12.90 fares, would be issued for train services with by Train and $80 for Shuttles |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/04/17/nyregion/nj-transit-world-cup-ticket-prices.html |work=The New York Times |url-access=limited |accessdate=April 26, Spain qualified for the 2026 World Cup after finishing first in its [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group E|qualification group]], and entered the tournament as the [[bookmaker]]s' favorite to win.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kallas |first=Fernando |date=November 18, 2025 |title=Spain qualify for World Cup after 2–2 draw with Turkey |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/spain-qualify-world-cup-after-2-2-draw-with-turkey-2025-11-18/ |work=Reuters |access-date=July 17, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260727165236/https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/spain-qualify-world-cup-after-2-2-draw-with-turkey-2025-11-18/|archive-date=July 27, 2026|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=June 12, 2025 |title=World Cup 2026 odds: Spain the favorite a year out from tournament |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/soccer/world-cup-2026-odds-france-opens-as-favorite-lines-for-usmnt |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251112154221/https://www.foxsports.com/stories/soccer/world-cup-2026-odds-france-opens-as-favorite-lines-for-usmnt |archive-date=November 12, 2025 |access-date=August 2, 2026 |website=[[FOX Sports]]}}</ref> Spain was drawn into [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group H|Group H]], alongside [[Cape Verde national football team|Cape Verde]], [[Saudi Arabia national football team|Saudi Arabia]], and [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 5, 2025 |title=Here are the groups for the 2026 FIFA World Cup |url=https://www.cnn.com/2025/12/05/sport/soccer-world-cup-2026-groups |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251205223844/https://edition.cnn.com/2025/12/05/sport/soccer-world-cup-2026-groups |archive-date=December 5, 2025 |access-date=July 29, 2026 |website=CNN}}</ref> Its first match was against Cape Verde in [[Atlanta]] on June 15. The game ended in a goalless draw, due to a strong defensive performance from Cape Verde and its goalkeeper, [[Vozinha]].<ref name="CNN-CPV">{{cite news |last1=Feldscher |first1=Kyle |last2=Riddell |first2=Don |date=June 15, 2026 |title=Tiny Cape Verde shocks favorite Spain with a draw in country's first World Cup match |url=https://www.cnn.com/2026/06/15/sport/cape-verde-spain-world-cup |publisher=[[CNN]] |accessdate=July 14, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260727165032/https://www.cnn.com/2026/06/15/sport/cape-verde-spain-world-cup|archive-date=July 27, 2026}}</ref> Spain's second match was against Saudi Arabia on June 21. [[Lamine Yamal]] gave Spain the lead ten minutes into the game, scoring his first World Cup goal from a cross by [[Mikel Oyarzabal]]. Oyarzabal added a second goal from a [[corner kick]] taken by Yamal, and within three minutes he scored again from [[Dani Olmo]]'s [[Header (association football)|header]] to give Spain a 3–0 halftime lead. In the second half, a [[Volley (association football)|volley]] by Spain's [[Marc Cucurella]] was saved by Saudi Arabian goalkeeper [[Hassan Tambakti|Hassan Al Tambakti]], but it deflected off [[Hassan Al-Tambakti|Hassan Al Tambakti]] for an [[own goal]] to seal Spain's 4–0 victory.{{Efn|Attributed to multiple references:<ref>{{Cite news |last=Brewin |first=John |date=June 21, 2026 |title=Spain 4-0 Saudi Arabia: World Cup 2026 – as it happened |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/jun/21/spain-v-saudi-arabia-world-cup-2026-live |access-date=July 23, 2026 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260621185214/https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/jun/21/spain-v-saudi-arabia-world-cup-2026-live|archive-date=June 21, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Lowe |first=Sid |author-link=Sid Lowe |date=June 21, 2026 |title=Lamine Yamal and Oyarzabal fire Spain to emphatic win against Saudi Arabia |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/21/spain-saudi-arabia-world-cup-group-h-match-report |work=[[The Guardian]] |accessdate=July 14, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260621204719/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/21/spain-saudi-arabia-world-cup-group-h-match-report|archive-date=June 21, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Howarth |first=Matthew |date=June 21, 2026 |title=Spain vs Saudi Arabia LIVE – June 21, 2026 |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c1eyg6lq5wvt |access-date=July 23, 2026 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260621234150/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c1eyg6lq5wvt|archive-date=June 21, 2026}}</ref>}} Spain's last group game was against Uruguay in [[Guadalajara]] on June 26. Spain won 1–0 after [[Álex Baena]]'s shot slipped through the hands of Uruguay goalkeeper [[Fernando Muslera]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lutz |first=Tom |date=June 26, 2026 |title=Uruguay's shock early exit ends with red card as Baena sends Spain through |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/27/uruguay-spain-world-cup-match-report |url-status=live |access-date=July 29, 2026 |website=The Guardian|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260627172209/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/27/uruguay-spain-world-cup-match-report|archive-date=June 27, 2026}}</ref> Spain advanced to the knockout stage as group winners with seven points.<ref name="Azzoni-2026">{{cite news |last=Azzoni |first=Tales |date=June 27, 2026 |title=Spain wins its World Cup group, beating Uruguay as Muslera's error sends 2-time champions home |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/worldcup/fifa-world-cup-uruguay-spain-recap-june-26-9.7248713 |work=CBC Sports |agency=Associated Press |accessdate=July 14, 2026 |archive-date=July 15, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260715045446/https://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/worldcup/fifa-world-cup-uruguay-spain-recap-june-26-9.7248713 |url-status=live }}</ref> [[File:Spain Starting XI France v Spain 7.24.26-029.jpg|thumb|Spain's starting lineup for the semifinal against France]]In the [[2026 FIFA World Cup round of 32|round of 32]], Spain faced [[Austria national football team|Austria]] at [[SoFi Stadium]] in [[Inglewood, California]] on July 2. Oyarzabal gave Spain a 1–0 lead in the 38th minute, scoring from a cross by Cucurella. In the second half, [[Pedro Porro]] scored Spain's second goal when he headed the ball from a cross by Baena. One minute before the end of regulation time, Oyarzabal added a third goal from a cross by Cucurella to seal a 3–0 win for Spain.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lowe |first=Sid |date=July 2, 2026 |title=Mikel Oyarzabal at the double as Spain beat Austria and cruise into last 16 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/jul/02/spain-v-austria-world-cup-2026-last-32-live |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260702225017/https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/jul/02/spain-v-austria-world-cup-2026-last-32-live |archive-date=July 2, 2026 |access-date=July 29, 2026 |website=The Guardian}}</ref><ref name="Smith-2026">{{cite news |last=Smith |first=Emma |date=July 2, 2026 |title=Spain 3–0 Austria: Mikel Oyarzabal scores twice in dominant win |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c8j2wvnzkvzt |work=BBC Sport |accessdate=July 14, 2026 |archive-date=July 4, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260704122957/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c8j2wvnzkvzt |url-status=live }}</ref> Spain's victory was its first in a World Cup knockout stage match since the [[2010 FIFA World Cup final|2010 final]].<ref name="Smith-2026" />

Spain faced [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]] in the [[2026 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Round of 16|round of 16]] at [[AT&T Stadium]] in [[Arlington, Texas|Arlington]], Texas on July 6. After a goalless first half, Spain's [[Mikel Merino]], who had come on as a [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]], scored the only goal of the game in second-half [[Association football#Duration and tie-breaking methods|stoppage time]] after receiving a pass from Torres.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Murray |first=Scott |date=July 6, 2026 |title=Portugal 0-1 Spain: World Cup 2026 last 16 – as it happened |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/jul/06/portugal-v-spain-world-cup-2026-last-16-live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260707205403/https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/jul/06/portugal-v-spain-world-cup-2026-last-16-live |archive-date=July 7, 2026 |access-date=August 2, 2026 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rajan |first=Adwaidh |date=July 6, 2026 |title=Portugal 0–1 Spain: Mikel Merino came off the bench to score an injury-time winner for Spain as they knocked Portugal - and Cristiano Ronaldo - out of the World Cup in a heavyweight last-16 tie in Dallas. |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cze9xg6480gt |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260706225010/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cze9xg6480gt |archive-date=July 6, 2026 |access-date=July 29, 2026 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> Spain faced [[Belgium national football team|Belgium]] in the quarterfinal in Inglewood on July 10. After Belgium goalkeeper [[Thibaut Courtois]] saved a shot from [[Dani Olmo]], [[Fabián Ruiz]] scored to give Spain a 1–0 lead. [[Charles De Ketelaere]] of Belgium equalized the score at 1–1 with a header from a cross by [[Timothy Castagne]] shortly before halftime. This was the only goal conceded by Spain in the tournament.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 19, 2026 |title=Fewest goals conceded in World Cup: Spain shutout makes history |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/fewest-goals-conceded-world-cup-195024858.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260720102723/https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/fewest-goals-conceded-world-cup-195024858.html |archive-date=July 20, 2026 |access-date=August 2, 2026 |website=Yahoo Sports |agency=USA Today}}</ref> In the second half, Courtois left the pitch injured and was replaced by [[Senne Lammens]]. After Lammens saved a 25 yards (23 m) shot from [[Pau Cubarsí|Pau Cubarsi]], Merino hit the rebound, scoring the winning goal two minutes before the end of regulation time to give Spain a 2–1 victory.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Munday |first=Billy |date=2026-07-10 |title=Spain 2-1 Belgium: World Cup 2026 quarter-final – as it happened |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/jul/10/spain-v-belgium-world-cup-2026-quarter-final-live |access-date=2026-07-29 |work=the Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rajan |first=Adwaidh |date=July 10, 2026 |title=Spain (2) {{!}} (1) Belgium – July 10, 2026 |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cjwgg64ennqt |access-date=July 29, 2026 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On July 14, Spain played [[France national football team|France]] in the semifinal in Dallas, and was awarded a penalty in the first half after Yamal was fouled by [[Lucas Digne]]. Oyarzabal took the penalty kick and scored to give Spain a 1–0 lead. In the 58th minute, Porro scored a second goal to give Spain a 2–0 win.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ames |first=Nick |date=July 14, 2026 |title=Spain reach World Cup final after Oyarzabal and Porro sink sorry France |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/14/france-spain-world-cup-semi-final-match-report |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260714211232/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/14/france-spain-world-cup-semi-final-match-report |archive-date=July 14, 2026 |access-date=July 29, 2026 |website=The Guardian}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Drury |first=Sam |date=July 14, 2026 |title=Superb Spain beat France to reach World Cup final |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cj3gdp4d3nnt#Report |work=BBC Sport |accessdate=July 14, 2026 |archive-date=July 14, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260714175419/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cj3gdp4d3nnt#Report |url-status=live }}</ref> Spain progressed to the final for the first time since 2010.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Spain reaches World Cup final with dominant 2-0 win over France |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/spain-beats-france-world-cup-final/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260714223652/https://www.cbsnews.com/news/spain-beats-france-world-cup-final/ |archive-date=July 14, 2026 |access-date=July 29, 2026 |website=CBS News}}</ref>

===Argentina===

Argentina earned its World Cup berth by placing first in [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONMEBOL)|South American qualifiers]], and entered the tournament also as one of the favorites to win.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Vickery |first1=Tim |last2=Becherano |first2=Lizzy |date=June 14, 2026 |title=Can Argentina really win the World Cup again? What stats and the players say |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49014778/can-argentina-really-win-world-cup-again-stats-players-say |publisher=ESPN |accessdate=July 15, 2026 |archive-date=July 16, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260716025919/https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49014778/can-argentina-really-win-world-cup-again-stats-players-say |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Rey |first1=Debora |last2=Savarese |first2=Mauricio |date=March 25, 2025 |title=Argentina secures a World Cup spot and then celebrates it with a 4–1 victory over archrival Brazil |url=https://apnews.com/article/argentina-world-cup-brazil-messi-6088e7977b166d279223c8f7176066fd |work=Associated Press |access-date=July 17, 2026 |archive-date=April 25, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260425061750/https://apnews.com/article/argentina-world-cup-brazil-messi-6088e7977b166d279223c8f7176066fd |url-status=live }}</ref> Argentina was drawn into [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group J|Group J]], alongside [[Algeria national football team|Algeria]], [[Austria national football team|Austria]], and [[Jordan national football team|Jordan]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Millar |first=Colin |date=December 5, 2025 |title=Argentina drawn in 2026 World Cup Group J: What to know about Algeria, Austria, Jordan |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6854719/2025/12/05/world-cup-draw-argentina-group-schedule-fixtures/ |work=The Athletic |url-access=subscription |accessdate=July 17, 2026 |archive-date=December 5, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251205191011/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6854719/2025/12/05/world-cup-draw-argentina-group-schedule-fixtures/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In its first match against Algeria at [[Arrowhead Stadium]] in [[Kansas City]] on June 16, Argentina won 3–0 through a [[List of FIFA World Cup hat-tricks|hat trick]] by [[Lionel Messi]]. Their second match was against Austria at AT&T Stadium on June 22. Argentina took the lead in the first half with a goal by Messi, who surpassed [[Miroslav Klose]] to become [[List of FIFA World Cup top goalscorers|the all-time top goalscorer]] at World Cup tournaments, with 17 goals. Messi added a second goal in second-half [[injury time]] to secure Argentina a 2–0 victory.<ref name="Ames-2026">{{cite news |last=Ames |first=Nick |date=June 22, 2026 |title=Irrepressible Messi breaks World Cup scoring record as Argentina beat Austria |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/22/argentina-austria-world-cup-group-j-match-report |work=The Guardian |accessdate=July 17, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260623004918/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/22/argentina-austria-world-cup-group-j-match-report|archive-date=June 23, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> Argentina’s last group game was against Jordan on June 27. Argentina won a free kick in the 19th minute, when [[Mohannad Abu Taha]] fouled [[Giovani Lo Celso]]. Celso took the kick and scored to give Argentina a 1–0 lead. After [[Nizar Al-Rashdan]] of Jordan fouled Argentina's [[Marcos Senesi]], [[Lautaro Martínez|Lautaro Martinez]] scored from the [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty]] kick in the 30th minute, giving Argentina a 2–0 lead. In the second half, [[Musa Al-Taamari]], who had come on as a substitute, scored once for Jordan to make the score 2–1. Messi took a free kick for Argentina after being fouled, and scored with a curling shot to give Argentina a 3–1 win. Argentina qualified as group winners with nine points.<ref>{{cite news |last=Drury |first=Sam |date=June 28, 2026 |title=Jordan 1–3 Argentina: Lionel Messi comes on to score sixth goal of World Cup 2026 |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c20ye67xgykt |work=BBC Sport |accessdate=July 17, 2026 |archive-date=July 16, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260716020659/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c20ye67xgykt |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Ames |first=Nick |date=June 28, 2026 |title=Lionel Messi steps off bench and makes a little more history in Argentina's World Cup win over Jordan |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/28/argentian-jordan-world-cup-group-j-match-report |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260628191232/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/28/argentian-jordan-world-cup-group-j-match-report |archive-date=June 28, 2026 |access-date=July 29, 2026 |website=The Guardian}}</ref>

[[File:P20260719DT-0633 President Donald J. Trump and First Lady Melania Trump attend the FIFA World Cup Final.jpg|thumb|Argentina's starting lineup during the final.]]Argentina faced Cape Verde in the round of 32 at [[Hard Rock Stadium]] on July 3. Argentina took the lead in the 29th minute when Messi scored from close range after a pass from [[Lisandro Martínez]]. In the second half, Cape Verde's [[Deroy Duarte]] equalized the score at 1–1 after receiving a cross from [[Ryan Mendes]]. The game went into [[Overtime (sports)|extra time]], where Argentina retook the lead after two minutes from a goal by Martínez, before [[Sidny Lopes Cabral]] of Cape Verde scored with a curling shot to even the score at 2–2 eleven minutes later. In the 111th minute, [[Cristian Romero]]'s header deflected off [[Diney (footballer, born 1995)|Diney Borges]]'s arm for an own goal, giving Argentina a 3–2 victory.<ref>{{cite news |last=Ronay |first=Barney |date=July 3, 2026 |title=Cape Verde threaten shock for the ages before Argentina break hearts in World Cup classic |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/04/argentina-cape-verde-world-cup-2026-last-32-match-report |work=The Guardian |accessdate=July 17, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260704012713/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/04/argentina-cape-verde-world-cup-2026-last-32-match-report|archive-date=July 4, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Coates |first=Charlotte |date=July 3, 2026 |title=Argentina 3–2 Cape Verde (AET): Messi through as holders survive scare to reach World Cup last 16 |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cz75y0v8qrjt |work=BBC Sport |accessdate=July 17, 2026 |archive-date=July 15, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260715200548/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cz75y0v8qrjt |url-status=live }}</ref> In the round of 16, Argentina played Egypt in Atlanta on July 7. Egypt took the lead after fifteen minutes when [[Yasser Ibrahim]] scored with a header from a corner kick taken by [[Mohamed Hany]]. After [[Mostafa Ziko]]'s goal was disallowed by the [[video assistant referee]] due to a foul, Ziko proceeded to score again in the second half to give Egypt a 2–0 lead.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Chutel |first1=Lynsey |last2=Khaled |first2=Rania |date=July 8, 2026 |title=Heartbreak and Anger in Egypt Over a Stinging World Cup Loss to Argentina |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/08/world/africa/egypt-argentina-goal-referee-conspiracy.html |work=The New York Times |url-access=subscription |accessdate=July 17, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260708192506/https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/08/world/africa/egypt-argentina-goal-referee-conspiracy.html|archive-date=July 8, 2026}}</ref> However, in what was described as "one of the great World Cup comebacks" by [[BBC Sport]], Argentina scored three goals in the final fifteen minutes—with a header by Romero, a goal by Messi, and a second header by [[Enzo Fernández]] to seal Argentina's 3–2 win.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Murray |first=Scott |date=July 7, 2026 |title=Argentina 3-2 Egypt: World Cup 2026 last 16 –as it happened |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/jul/07/argentina-v-egypt-world-cup-2026-last-16-live |access-date=August 1, 2026 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref name="BBC-EGY">{{cite news |last=Howarth |first=Matthew |date=July 7, 2026 |title=World Cup 2026 results: Argentina 3–2 Egypt as Lionel Messi scores after having penalty saved |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cdr4m2122lgt |work=BBC Sport |accessdate=July 17, 2026 |archive-date=July 10, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260710205208/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cdr4m2122lgt |url-status=live }}</ref>

Argentina's quarterfinal was against [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland]] in Kansas City on July 11. Argentina took the lead after ten minutes when [[Alexis Mac Allister]] scored with a header. The match was tied at 1–1 in the 67th minute by [[Dan Ndoye]] of Switzerland.<ref name="ABC-SUI">{{cite news |last=Skretta |first=Dave |date=July 11, 2026 |title=Argentina beats Switzerland 3–1 in extra time, advancing to World Cup semifinals |url=https://abcnews.com/Sports/wireStory/argentina-lineup-unchanged-messi-alongside-alvarez-world-cup-134686135 |work=ABC News |agency=Associated Press |accessdate=July 17, 2026 |archive-date=July 14, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260714104253/https://abcnews.com/Sports/wireStory/argentina-lineup-unchanged-messi-alongside-alvarez-world-cup-134686135 |url-status=live }}</ref> Five minutes later, [[Breel Embolo]] of Switzerland was [[Fouls and misconduct (association football)#Red card (dismissal)|sent off]] after being given a second yellow card for [[Diving (association football)|diving]]. Argentina eventually won 3–1 in extra time through a long-distance strike by [[Julián Alvarez]] and a rebound from Lautaro Martínez.<ref name="ABC-SUI" /><ref>{{cite news |last=Ames |first=Nick |date=July 11, 2026 |title=Julián Álvarez's extra-time stunner sinks 10-man Switzerland to send Argentina into semi-finals |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/12/switzerland-argentina-world-cup-quarter-final-match-report |work=The Guardian |accessdate=July 17, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260712042834/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/12/switzerland-argentina-world-cup-quarter-final-match-report|archive-date=July 12, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> Argentina advanced to the semifinal on July 15 in Atlanta, where it faced [[England national football team|England]], a [[Argentina–England football rivalry|longtime rival]] in the World Cup.<ref>{{cite news |last=Alcoba |first=Natalie |date=July 15, 2026 |title=Old rivals, new battle: Argentina and England clash in World Cup Semifinal |url=https://www.npr.org/2026/07/15/nx-s1-5893686/old-rivals-new-battle-argentina-and-england-clash-in-world-cup-semi-final |publisher=NPR |accessdate=July 17, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260715145909/https://www.npr.org/2026/07/15/nx-s1-5893686/old-rivals-new-battle-argentina-and-england-clash-in-world-cup-semifinal|archive-date=July 15, 2026}}</ref> After [[Anthony Gordon (footballer)|Anthony Gordon]]'s goal in the 55th minute gave England the lead, England head coach [[Thomas Tuchel]] switched to a five-defender formation with several substitutions.<ref name="Guardian-ENG">{{cite news |last=Hytner |first=David |date=July 15, 2026 |title=Argentina's late double breaks England hearts in dramatic World Cup semi-final |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/15/england-argentina-world-cup-semi-final-match-report |work=The Guardian |accessdate=July 17, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260715215206/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/15/england-argentina-world-cup-semi-final-match-report|archive-date=July 15, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Hamilton |first=Tom |date=July 16, 2026 |title=Tuchel's retreat set up England's World Cup exit as Argentina smelled blood |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49373334/tuchel-retreat-set-england-world-cup-exit-argentina-smelt-blood |publisher=ESPN |accessdate=July 17, 2026 |archive-date=July 16, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260716083957/https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49373334/tuchel-retreat-set-england-world-cup-exit-argentina-smelt-blood |url-status=live }}</ref> Messi provided assists for Fernández's equalizing goal in the 86th minute and for Martínez's game-winning header goal in the second minute of stoppage time. Argentina won 2–1 to reach their second consecutive World Cup final.<ref name="Guardian-ENG" />

==Pre-match==

=== Officiating ===
On July 16, 2026, [[Slavko Vinčić]] of Slovenia was named as the [[Referee (association football)|referee]] for the final, with fellow Slovenians Tomaž Klančnik and Andraž Kovačič as [[Assistant referee (association football)#Assistant referee|assistant referees]]. [[Adham Makhadmeh]] and Mohammad Al-Kalaf of Jordan were named as the fourth [[Assistant referee (association football)#Fourth official|official]] and [[Assistant referee (association football)#Fifth official and reserve assistant referee|reserve assistant referee]], respectively. The VAR team consisted of [[Bastian Dankert]], [[Nicolás Gallo (referee)|Nicolas Gallo]], and [[Khamis Al-Marri]]. [[Tatiana Guzmán|Tatiana Guzman]] and Guillermo Pacheco served as standby VARs.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Singh |first=Pragjyoti |date=July 19, 2026 |title=Who Is the Referee In Spain vs. Argentina World Cup Final Match? |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/referee-spain-vs-argentina-world-184500511.html |access-date=July 21, 2026 |website=Yahoo Sports |language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260721200857/https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/referee-spain-vs-argentina-world-184500511.html|archive-date=July 21, 2026|url-status=live|agency=[[Parade Media]]}}</ref> Earlier in the 2026 World Cup, Vinčić officiated the Brazil–Morocco and Jordan–Algeria matches in the group stage and the Mexico–Ecuador match in the round of 32.<ref name="ESPN-Referee2">{{cite news |date=July 17, 2026|title=Who is Slavko Vincic? Spain vs. Argentina referee for World Cup final drew Real Madrid backlash, Jose Mourinho praise|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49382615/who-slavko-vincic-spain-vs-argentina-referee-world-cup-final-real-madrid-jose-mourinho-jude-bellingham|publisher=ESPN|accessdate=July 17, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260718111828/https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49382615/who-slavko-vincic-spain-vs-argentina-referee-world-cup-final-real-madrid-jose-mourinho-jude-bellingham|archive-date=July 18, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="FIFA-2026">{{cite press release |date=July 16, 2026|title=Slovenian Slavko Vinčić to take charge of FIFA World Cup 2026 final|url=https://inside.fifa.com/refereeing/news/slavko-vincic-world-cup-2026-final-referee-spain-argentina|publisher=FIFA|accessdate=July 17, 2026|archive-date=July 17, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260717063616/https://inside.fifa.com/refereeing/news/slavko-vincic-world-cup-2026-final-referee-spain-argentina|url-status=live}}</ref> He had previously officiated the [[2022 UEFA Europa League final]] and [[2024 UEFA Champions League final]]. He was also one of the referees at the [[UEFA Euro 2020]], [[2022 FIFA World Cup|2022 World Cup]], [[UEFA Euro 2024]], and [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup]]. He became the first Slovenian to referee a World Cup final.<ref name="FIFA-2026" />

===Dignitaries in attendance===
US president [[Donald Trump]] and First Lady [[Melania Trump]] attended the final with [[United States Secretary of State|secretary of state]] [[Marco Rubio]], along with Mexican president [[Claudia Sheinbaum]], Canadian prime minister [[Mark Carney]], and New Jersey Governor [[Mikie Sherrill]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Rampling |first1=Ali |last2=Tansley |first2=Eduardo |date=July 17, 2026 |title=World Cup winners to be presented with championship rings in tournament first |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7451605/2026/07/17/world-cup-winners-championship-rings/ |work=The Athletic |url-access=subscription |accessdate=July 17, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260718134531/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7451605/2026/07/17/world-cup-winners-championship-rings/|archive-date=July 18, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Orozco |first1=Jose |last2=Hilarie |first2=Valentine |date=July 17, 2026 |title=Sheinbaum, Carney to Watch World Cup Final With Trump with ordinary Mexicans unable to afford tickets, but decided to attend the final after receiving a direct invitation from Trump.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mexico's Sheinbaum to Attend World Cup Final at |title=Superstitious Argentine president Milei won't attend World Cup final |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49380261/argentina-president-javier-milei-attend-2026-world-cup-final Association]] (AFA).<ref>{{Cite news |date=July 20, 2026 |title=FIFA World Cup 2026: CONMEBOL chief Alejandro Dominguez meets US Secretary of State Marco Rubio during Argentina vs Spain final |url=https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/afa-president/fifa-world-cup-2026-conmebol-chief-alejandro-dominguez-meets-us-secretary-of-state-marco-rubio-during-argentina-vs-spain-final |work=[[The Tribune |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/trump-and-mamdani-plan-to-attend-world-cup-final-on-sunday/ |access-date=August 3, 2026 |website=The Seattle Times |language=en-US |agency=The New York Times}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Dunbar |first=Graham |date=July 24, 2026 |title=IOC won't pursue its member Infantino over FIFA red-card ruling at World Cup |url=https://abcnews.com/Sports/wireStory/ioc-pursue-member-infantino-fifa-red-card-ruling-135059599 |access-date=August 3, 2026 |website=ABC News |language=en |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

Although [[UEFA]] President [[Aleksander Čeferin]] attended the tournament's [[2026 FIFA World Cup opening ceremonies|June 11 opening match in Mexico City]], he boycotted the final after a [[2026 Trump–FIFA red card controversy|dispute with FIFA over a suspended disciplinary ban]] issued to [[United States men's national soccer team|United States]] player [[Folarin Balogun]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Rumsby |first=Ben |date=July 20, 2026 |title=Uefa president boycotts World Cup final after Fifa's role in Balogun saga |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2026/07/20/uefa-president-boycotts-world-cup-final/ |access-date=July 20, 2026 |work=[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]] (UK)|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260721020206/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2026/07/20/uefa-president-boycotts-world-cup-final/|archive-date=July 21, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> Čeferin, representing the European confederation of which Spain is a member, criticized FIFA's decision to defer Balogun's automatic suspension after he received a red card during a round of 32 match against [[Bosnia and Herzegovina national football team|Bosnia and Herzegovina]], which the United States won 2–0.<ref>{{Cite news |date=July 20, 2026 |title=Aleksander Ceferin boycotts World Cup final after Folarin Balogun scandal |url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/football/world-cup/article/aleksander-ceferin-boycott-world-cup-final-folarin-balogun-ts6dfjk87 |work=[[The Times]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260720221228/https://www.thetimes.com/sport/football/world-cup/article/aleksander-ceferin-boycott-world-cup-final-folarin-balogun-ts6dfjk87|archive-date=July 20, 2026|access-date=July 20, 2026|url-status=live|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

=== Air quality concerns ===
There were concerns that smoke from the [[2026 Canadian wildfires|ongoing Canadian wildfires]] would affect the air quality of the final and impact player performance. Spain decided to practice under the smoke, while Argentina practiced in Atlanta to avoid the smoke. FIFA President [[Gianni Infantino]] met with Trump and [[FIFA World Cup 2026 Task Force|World Cup Task Force]] leader [[Andrew Giuliani]] to discuss the wildfires.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Whyno|first=Stephen|date=2026-07-17|title=Uncertainty clouds the forecast on whether wildfire smoke will affect the World Cup final|url=https://apnews.com/article/world-cup-final-smoke-76edbb6afca0501747d8ebaf91a741fc|access-date=2026-08-15|website=[[Associated Press]]|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Whyno|first=Stephen|last2=Borenstein|first2=Seth|date=2026-07-16|title=Spain practices outside before the World Cup final as smoke fills the air in northern New Jersey|url=https://apnews.com/article/spain-wildfires-smoke-world-cup-c2fc1c37a64bb6514708052dc5e42d28|access-date=2026-08-15|website=[[Associated Press]]|language=en}}</ref> At the time, New York and New Jersey were under air quality alerts, and air quality readings in New York City were deemed "very unhealthy" and well above levels deemed dangerous to the general public.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tawfik|first=Nada|date=2026-07-16|title=New York issues air quality alert days before World Cup final|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c9w0jen8x90o|access-date=2026-08-15|website=BBC Sport|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Feeley|first=Jack|last2=Kindelan|first2=Katie|last3=Gewecke|first3=Kenton|date=2026-07-17|title=Authorities 'monitoring' wildfires' impact on 2026 World Cup final, sources say|url=https://abcnews.com/GMA/News/wildfires-air-quality-impact-2026-world-cup-final/story?id=134848966|access-date=2026-08-15|website=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]]|language=en}}</ref> The day prior to the final, much of the smoke dissipated due to heavy thunderstorms, and the air quality improved to the point where there was no risk to the general public.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-07-18|title=Storms expected to clear wildfire smoke ahead of World Cup final|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49392587/storms-due-clear-wildfire-smoke-world-cup-final-spain-argentina|access-date=2026-08-15|website=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref>

==Match==

=== First half ===
[[File:Lisandro Martinez Dani Olmo Argentina v Spain 19 July 2026-097.jpg|thumb|right|Action during the first half]]
Argentina kicked off the match at 3:06&nbsp;p.m. [[Eastern Time Zone|EDT]] (7:06&nbsp;p.m. [[Coordinated Universal Time|UTC]]) in front of a crowd of 80,663. The weather at [[Teterboro Airport]], {{convert|4.4|mi|km|abbr=on}} from the stadium,{{efn|Distance measured using Google Maps distance calculator, between Teterboro Airport, coordinates {{Coord|40.8501|N|74.0608|W}} and MetLife Stadium, coordinates {{Coord|40.8135|N|74.0743|W}}<ref>{{Google maps |url=https://www.google.com/maps/place/Teterboro+Airport/@40.858332,-74.0641041,17z |access-date=July 19, 2026 |title=Teterboro Airport}}</ref><ref>{{Google maps |url=https://www.google.com/maps/place/New+York+New+Jersey+Stadium/@40.8135064,-74.0770319,17z |access-date=July 19, 2026 |title=New York New Jersey Stadium}}</ref>}} was recorded as fair before kick-off, with a temperature of 80&nbsp;°F (27&nbsp;°C) and 40% humidity.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Teterboro, NJ Weather History – July 19, 2026|url=https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/us/nj/teterboro/KTEB/date/2026-7-19|url-status=|access-date=July 19, 2026|website=[[The Weather Company]]|date=July 19, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260720194130/https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/us/nj/teterboro/KTEB/date/2026-7-19|archive-date=July 20, 2026}}</ref> Five minutes into the game, [[Lamine Yamal]] had a chance to score for Spain when he received a pass from [[Dani Olmo]]. He took a shot that deflected off [[Lisandro Martínez|Lisandro Martinez]]'s foot and was saved by Argentina's goalkeeper, [[Emiliano Martínez]]. [[Julián Alvarez|Julián Álvarez]] of Argentina attempted to pass the ball to [[Lionel Messi]], but Spain's goalkeeper [[Unai Simón]] ran 40 yards (36.5 m) from the goal to outpace him and kick it away. In the 11th minute, Yamal attempted to receive the ball from a cross by [[Rodri (footballer, born 1996)|Rodri]], but it went out of the [[Out of bounds|touchline]]. A minute later, Spain won a [[corner kick]] after [[Fabián Ruiz]]'s shot was deflected by Emiliano Martínez in the [[penalty area]].<ref name=":02" />

Two minutes later, [[Alexis Mac Allister]] of Argentina fouled Dani Olmo.<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |last=McNulty |first=Phil |date=July 19, 2026 |title=Spain 1-0 Argentina: Ferran Torres scores as Spain win World Cup for second time |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cgk4ymn3n72t |access-date=August 4, 2026 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> In the 15th minute, Argentina won a free kick 45 yards (41.1 m) from Spain's goal after Messi was [[Glossary of association football terms#Tackle|tackled]] by [[Álex Baena|Alex Baena]]. [[Rodrigo De Paul]]'s kick went over the [[Glossary of association football terms#W|wall]] and was saved by Simón. In the 39th minute, Spain's [[Mikel Oyarzabal]] received a pass from [[Fabián Ruiz]] outside of the penalty area and made a 20-yard (18 m) low shot at the goal, but it was saved by Emiliano Martínez. In the 41st minute, Lisandro Martínez was given a [[Penalty card|yellow card]] for a foul on Oyarzabal, and a minute later a left-footed shot from [[Marc Cucurella]] went wide of the goal. Argentina was forced to make a [[Substitute (association football)|substitution]] after Lisandro Martínez became injured, with [[Nicolás Otamendi]] taking his place.<ref name=":12">{{Cite news |last=Smyth |first=Rob |date=July 20, 2026 |title=Spain beat Argentina 1–0 after extra time to win the 2026 World Cup – as it happened |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/jul/19/spain-v-argentina-world-cup-2026-final-live-updates |access-date=July 20, 2026 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref name=":02" />

=== Second half ===
The second half began with a substitution from Argentina, with [[Leandro Paredes]] replacing [[Nicolás González (footballer, born 1998)|Nicolás Gonzalez]]. One minute later, Baena made a 22-yard (20 m) shot towards Argentina's goal which was saved by Emiliano Martínez. Paredes received a yellow card for pushing Rodri. In the 57th minute, Argentina brought [[Nahuel Molina]] onto the pitch in place of [[Gonzalo Montiel]]. In the 60th minute, Spain won a free kick when Paredes fouled [[Pedro Porro]] 25 yards (23 m) from Argentina's goal. Yamal took the kick and hit the [[Glossary of association football terms#Wall|wall]]. Spain then made two substitutions, with [[Pedri]] and [[Ferran Torres]] coming on in place of Ruiz and Oyarzabal, respectively. In the 64th minute, Olmo hit a 22-yard (20 m) shot that deflected off Martinez and went wide of the goalpost. Three minutes later, Spain had what [[Chris Sutton]] described as a "golden opportunity" when Yamal delivered a cross to Torres, who hit a goal-bound [[Header (association football)|header]] that was saved by Martínez. In the 70th minute, Argentina made two substitutions when [[Giuliano Simeone]] and [[Facundo Medina]] replaced [[Rodrigo De Paul|De Paul]] and [[Cristian Romero]], respectively. Five minutes later, Spain sent [[Nico Williams]] and [[Mikel Merino]] onto the pitch in place of Baena and Olmo. In the 77th minute, Pedri made a shot from the edge of the penalty area, but it was saved by Martínez. [[Pau Cubarsí|Cubarsí]] then struck a 25-yard (23 m) shot at Argentina's goal, which Martinez saved with a dive.<ref name=":12"/><ref name=":02" />[[File:Enzo Fernandez Pau Cubarsi Argentina v Spain 19 July 2026-208.jpg |thumb|Enzo Fernández of Argentina received a second yellow card after tackling Pau Cubarsí]]In the 80th minute, Nico Williams made a cross that [[Aymeric Laporte]] tried to meet with a header, but Martínez caught the ball.<ref name="MTresumen">{{Cite news |last=Figueroa |first=Juan Manuel |date=July 19, 2026 |title=¡Furia Roja! España destronó a Messi y a Argentina y es Campeón del Mundial 2026 |url=https://www.mediotiempo.com/futbol/copa-mundial/resumen-partido-espana-vs-argentina-1-0-final-mundial-2026 |work=Mediotiempo |language=es|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260719224932/https://www.mediotiempo.com/futbol/copa-mundial/resumen-partido-espana-vs-argentina-1-0-final-mundial-2026|archive-date=July 19, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> In the 82nd minute, Argentina's [[Enzo Fernández]] fell to the ground following contact from [[Rodri]], and the referee did not award a foul, leading Fernández to complain and then receive a yellow card for dissent. In the 3rd minute of [[stoppage time]], Argentina's [[Giuliano Simeone]] made a low cross from the right, but [[Unai Simón]] intercepted the ball. On the resulting counterattack, Williams dribbled the ball for 30 meters before taking a shot from the edge of the [[Glossary of association football terms#Penalty area|box]], which was also saved by Martínez.<ref name="MTresumen" /> A few minutes later, Fernández was [[Fouls and misconduct (association football)|sent off]] after receiving a second yellow card for tackling Pau Cubarsí while attempting to win a loose ball; a VAR review upheld the on-field decision.<ref>{{cite web |title=World Cup VAR review: Why Fernandez red card was deserved as Argentina lose World Cup final|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49027532/world-cup-2026-var-review-red-card-penalty-handball-goal-line-technology|work=ESPN|date=2026-07-19}}</ref>.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Corcuera |first1=Álvaro |last2=Pineda |first2=Rafael |last3=Benítez |first3=J. M. |last4=Muñoz |first4=Mikel |date=July 19, 2026 |title=Así te hemos contado la victoria de España en la final del Mundial ante Argentina para proclamarse campeona |url=https://elpais.com/deportes/mundial-futbol/2026-07-19/espana-argentina-en-directo-la-final-del-mundial-en-vivo.html |work=[[El País]] |language=es}}</ref> In the final seconds of regulation time, Yamal struck a free kick that Martínez managed to deflect away.<ref name="MTresumen" /> As regulation time concluded, Argentina became the first team to fail to register a shot during the first 90 minutes of a World Cup final.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Lopesino |first1=Juan |last2=Nelson |first2=David |date=July 19, 2026 |title=Argentina's first 90 minutes against Spain: 0.00 xG and no shots on target |url=https://en.as.com/soccer/world-cup/argentinas-first-90-minutes-against-spain-000-xg-and-no-shots-on-target-f202607-n/ |access-date=July 20, 2026 |website=AS USA |language=en-us}}</ref>

=== Extra time ===
[[File: Ferran Torres Argentina v Spain 19 July 2026-233.jpg|thumb|Ferran Torres of Spain, after scoring the game's only goal]]
In the 93rd minute of the match during [[extra time]], Williams was not able to head a [[Pedri]] cross with enough power, and Martínez dove to his right to make the save.<ref name="Bencid-2026">{{Cite news |last=Bencid |first=Abraham |date=July 19, 2026 |title=España vs Argentina: resumen, goles en video y resultado de la gran final del Mundial 2026 |url=https://www.clarosports.com/futbol/mundial-2026/espana-vs-argentina-en-vivo-la-final-del-mundial-2026-resultado-y-goles-del-partido-messi-vs-lamine-yamal-hoy-19-de-julio/ |work=[[Claro Sports]] |language=Spanish|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260720234210/https://www.clarosports.com/futbol/mundial-2026/espana-vs-argentina-en-vivo-la-final-del-mundial-2026-resultado-y-goles-del-partido-messi-vs-lamine-yamal-hoy-19-de-julio/|archive-date=July 20, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> Three minutes later, Williams appeared to score, but the goal was disallowed because Merino had stepped on Otamendi's foot. Commentators noted that the contact was minor and was the type that referees sometimes overlook in the penalty area, and also observed that Otamendi had his arm around Merino prior to the incident.{{efn|Attributed to multiple references:<ref>{{Cite news |last=Cons |first=Roddy |date=July 19, 2026 |title=Nico Williams goal disallowed in Spain vs Argentina World Cup final: Why was it ruled out? |url=https://en.as.com/soccer/world-cup/nico-williams-goal-disallowed-in-spain-vs-argentina-world-cup-final-why-was-it-ruled-out-f202607-n/ |work=[[Diario AS]]}}</ref><ref name="1.a.3">{{Cite web |title=Spain left 'perplexed' and 'bemused' after disallowed goal: 'It's a clear and obvious error'|url=https://football360.com.au/spain-argentina-fifa-world-cup-final-disallowed-goal-why-details-reaction/|access-date=July 21, 2026 |website=Football360|language=en}}</ref><ref name="1.a.4">{{Cite web |title=Spain fans rage after VAR chalks off Nico Williams' World Cup final goal|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/football/story/world-cup-final-nico-williams-var-controversy-mikel-merino-nicolas-otamendi-2951624-2026-07-20|access-date=July 21, 2026 |website=[[India Today]]|language=en}}</ref>}} Spain supporters sarcastically chanted "Infantino" following the disallowed goal, referencing allegations of FIFA favoring Argentina.<ref name="1.a.3" />

Merino then headed the ball wide of Argentina's goal in the 102nd minute. At the start of the second period of extra time, Torres received a ball headed by Williams. He struck it with his left foot from close range and past Martínez, scoring the first goal of the match and putting Spain in the lead 1–0.<ref name="MTresumen" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cgk4ymn3n72t|title= Spain 1 Argentina 0 (AET)|date=July 19, 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=July 22, 2026}}</ref>

After Spain's goal, Argentina began to counterattack in search of an [[Glossary of association football terms#Equaliser|equalizer goal]]. In the 113th minute, Torres appeared to score his second goal, but it was ruled out for being offside. Two minutes later, Messi attempted to catch Simón off guard with a cross that drifted toward the Spanish goal, passing over the crossbar. In the 116th minute, Williams positioned himself in Argentina's box after outrunning [[Nahuel Molina]], but was unable to connect with the ball to shoot. A minute later, Messi made Argentina's first shot from the edge of the box, which struck Merino in the face as he blocked it, leaving him down on the pitch.<ref name="Bencid-2026" /><ref>{{cite web |author= [[The Athletic]]|date= July 19, 2026|title= Lionel Messi had Argentina's first shot of the World Cup final after 116 minutes. It was blocked by the head of Mikel Merino.|url= https://x.com/TheAthleticFC/status/2078978440087409066|website= [[X (social network)]]|access-date=July 20, 2026}}</ref>

In the 120th minute, Argentina's final attack came from a [[Giuliano Simeone]] pass toward [[Marcos Senesi]] in the box, but Cubarsí cleared the ball.<ref>{{cite web|last= Cervelló Herrero |first= Laia |date=July 20, 2026 |title= Pau Cubarsi, the World Cup's best youngster who plays like a veteran but looks like an angel |url= https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7458228/2026/07/20/pau-cubarsi-world-cup-young-player-barcelona/ |website= [[The New York Times]]|access-date = July 20, 2026}}</ref> The resulting corner kick led to a scramble inside the goal area, with the Spanish defense kicking the ball out of bounds. The next corner kick was deflected by Argentina's [[Nicolás Tagliafico]] on the near post and fell to Simeone's feet, but his shot from close to the penalty spot went well over the crossbar.<ref>{{cite web |last= Zavala|first= Jaime|date= July 20, 2026|title= Simeone, villano en la final argentina: falló un gol y en España optó por subirse las calcetas |url= https://www.canal9.cl/episodios/2026/07/20/simeone-el-villano-de-final-en-argentina-erro-gol-y-prefirio-subirse-las-calcetas-en-tanto-de-espana|website= Canal 9 Bío Bío Televisión|access-date= July 20, 2026}}</ref> In the final minutes, Spain kept possession away from its goal. A long free kick from Emiliano Martinez into Spain's goal area was cleared by its defense before the final whistle confirmed Spain's victory.<ref name="Bencid-2026" />
