==Post-match==
[[File:Pau Cubarsi Rodri Unai Simon Argentina v Spain 19 July 2026-298.jpg|thumb|Spain's players with their awards, pictured from left to right: Pau Cubarsí (Young Player Award), Rodri (Golden Ball), and Unai Simón (Golden Glove)]]
Spain's [[Ferran Torres]], who scored the only goal of the final, was named as the [[man of the match]].<ref name="MOTM" /> In the awards ceremony after the match, Spain's Rodri was awarded the [[FIFA World Cup Golden Ball|Golden Ball]] as the best player of the tournament, while his teammate [[Unai Simón]] was awarded the [[FIFA World Cup Golden Glove|Golden Glove]] as the best goalkeeper. Spain's [[Pau Cubarsí]] won the [[FIFA World Cup Young Player Award|FIFA Young Player Award]] as the best young player of the tournament. [[Lionel Messi]] won the Silver Ball as the second-best player of the tournament, and the Silver Boot as the second-top goalscorer, with eight goals.<ref>{{cite web |title=FIFA World Cup awards: Rodri, Cubarsi, Simon and Mbappe honoured |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/award-winners |publisher=[[FIFA]] |date=July 19, 2026}}</ref> FIFA president [[Gianni Infantino]] and US president [[Donald Trump]] were booed by some spectators as they entered the field with the World Cup trophy, which they presented to Spain's captain [[Rodri (footballer, born 1996)|Rodri]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Bushnell |first=Henry |date=July 19, 2026 |title=Trump booed by World Cup final crowd, takes part in trophy presentation |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7455328/2026/07/19/trump-booed-world-cup-final/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260720005147/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7455328/2026/07/19/trump-booed-world-cup-final/ |archive-date=July 20, 2026 |access-date=July 20, 2026 |work=[[The Athletic]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Abnos |first=Alexander |date=July 19, 2026 |title=Donald Trump and Gianni Infantino booed before US president attempts to crash Spain celebrations |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/19/donald-trump-world-cup-final |access-date=July 19, 2026 |website=The Guardian}}</ref>

[[Lamine Yamal]] and Messi embraced after the match, a moment described by FIFA and several media outlets as symbolic of a generational transition in football, with Messi approaching the end of an illustrious career and Yamal, regarded as one of the sport's most promising talents, at the start of his.<ref name="2007photo">{{Cite news |date=July 19, 2026 |title=How fresh Messi-Yamal image signals changing of the guard |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/how-fresh-messi-yamal-image-signals-changing-of-the-guard |work=[[FIFA]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260721003339/https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/how-fresh-messi-yamal-image-signals-changing-of-the-guard|archive-date=July 21, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=McNulty |first=Phil |date=July 20, 2026 |title=Lamine Yamal 'completes football' at 19 as Argentina betray Messi |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c0m7zx38v43o |work=[[BBC News]]}}</ref> The encounter drew additional resonance from [[2007 Messi–Yamal photo shoot|a 2007 photograph]] in which Messi, then 20 years old, bathed the infant Yamal during a charity photo session while at [[FC Barcelona]]. The image had attracted renewed media attention as the two players prepared to face each other in the 2026 World Cup final.<ref name="2007photo" />

Spain became the first country to simultaneously hold both the men's and women's World Cup titles, having won the Women's World Cup in [[2023 FIFA Women's World Cup|2023]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Litman |first=Laken |date=July 19, 2026 |title=How Spain's Men's And Women's National Teams Rose Above The Rest Of The World |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/soccer/world-cup-spain-men-women-lamine-yamal-aitana-bonmati-alexia-putellas |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260720004454/https://www.foxsports.com/stories/soccer/world-cup-spain-men-women-lamine-yamal-aitana-bonmati-alexia-putellas |archive-date=July 20, 2026 |access-date=July 20, 2026 |website=[[Fox Sports]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Singh |first=Abhishek |date=July 20, 2026 |title=Spain become 1st nation to simultaneously hold men's and women's FIFA World Cup titles |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/sports/spain-become-1st-nation-to-simultaneously-hold-mens-and-womens-fifa-world-cup-titles/4296756/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260720004637/https://www.financialexpress.com/sports/spain-become-1st-nation-to-simultaneously-hold-mens-and-womens-fifa-world-cup-titles/4296756/ |archive-date=July 20, 2026 |access-date=July 20, 2026 |website=[[The Financial Express (India)|The Financial Express]] |language=en}}</ref> Spain also became the second European nation to win a World Cup held in the [[Americas]], following [[Germany national football team|Germany]] in [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=García García |first=Sergio |date=19 July 2026 |title=North and South America remain a curse for European teams: This is the only country to win the World Cup in the Americas |url=https://en.as.com/soccer/world-cup/north-and-south-america-remain-a-curse-for-european-teams-this-is-the-only-country-to-win-the-world-cup-in-the-americas-f202607-n/ |work=[[Diario AS]] |publication-place=Madrid, Spain}}</ref> Messi became the second player in history to play in three World Cup finals, after [[Cafu]] of [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]].<ref>{{cite news |date=July 19, 2026 |title=Lionel Messi Becomes Second-Ever Player To Appear In 3 Men's World Cup Finals |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/soccer/lionel-messi-becomes-second-ever-player-appear-3-mens-world-cup-finals |work=Fox Sports |accessdate=July 19, 2026}}</ref> The 2026 final featured 11 saves by Argentina goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez, the most ever recorded in a World Cup final.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Chavkin |first=Daniel |date=July 19, 2026 |title=Most saves in a World Cup final: Where Emiliano Martinez's stellar goalkeeping vs. Spain ranks in FIFA history |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/most-saves-world-cup-final-212715455.html |work=[[The Sporting News]] |via=[[Yahoo Sports]]}}</ref>

===Altercations between players===
After the match concluded, multiple altercations broke out between Argentina's and Spain's players.<ref>{{cite web |last=Heverin|first=Dane|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/football/fifa-world-cup-final-2026-argentinas-leandro-paredes-grabs-spains-eric-garcia-by-the-throat-nahuel-molina-attacks-spanish-substitutes-punches-thrown-after-final-whistle-in-violent-scenes/news-story/5c73f68b2cf92b31b1212df3594177d7|title='Sore loser': Argentina slammed over 'disgusting' act as coach makes astonishing World Cup Final claim|work=Fox Sports|date=July 20, 2026}}</ref> Argentina's defender [[Nahuel Molina]] was seen striking Spain's captain [[Rodri (footballer, born 1996)|Rodri]] in the stomach, who was running to celebrate his team's victory. Shortly after, Argentina's [[Leandro Paredes]] tackled [[Eric Garcia (footballer, born 2001)|Eric Garcia]], who fell to the ground, resulting in a physical altercation. Just as he was getting up, Paredes shoved him by the throat, and shortly after, Argentina's [[coaching staff]] protected Garcia from him. Paredes then wrestled [[Gavi (footballer)|Gavi]] to the ground, with substitute [[Thiago Almada]] getting involved as he ripped his training bib.<ref name="guardian 2026-07-20">{{cite web |last=Hughes|first=Matt|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/20/argentina-players-face-bans-as-fifa-opens-investigation-into-world-cup-final-brawls|title=Argentina players face bans as Fifa opens investigation into World Cup final brawls|work=The Guardian|date=July 20, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Pinner |first=Joe |date=July 20, 2026 |title=Gangs of New Jersey: how the World Cup final descended into ugly scenes between Argentina and Spain |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/20/gangs-of-new-jersey-how-the-world-cup-final-descended-into-ugly-scenes-between-argentina-and-spain |access-date=July 21, 2026 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=England|first=Adam|url=https://people.com/world-cup-final-brawl-punches-thrown-argentina-player-grabs-spanish-opponent-by-throat-12022317|title=World Cup Final Ends in Brawl as Punches Are Thrown and Argentina Player Grabs Spanish Opponent by the Throat|work=People|date=July 20, 2026}}</ref> Argentina's assistant coach [[Roberto Ayala]] grabbed Spain's [[Dani Olmo]] by the bib before punching him in the face.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://onefootball.com/en/news/video-raton-ayalas-shock-punch-on-dani-olmo-after-the-final-whistle-43162030 |title=VIDEO {{!}} Ratón Ayala's shock punch on Dani Olmo after the final whistle |work=OneFootball |date=July 20, 2026 }} {{Dead link|date=October 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rodriguez |first=Jose Victor Escobar |date=July 20, 2026 |title=Roberto Ayala caught hitting Dani Olmo during the chaotic World Cup Final brawl |url=https://www.marca.com/en/world-cup/2026/07/20/roberto-ayala-caught-hitting-dani-olmo-during-the-chaotic-world-cup-final-brawl.html |access-date=July 21, 2026 |website=Marca |language=en-US}}</ref> Multiple media outlets claimed that Paredes was shown a red card after the brawl,<ref>Multiple sources:
*{{Cite web |last=Braidwood |first=Jaime |date=July 20, 2026 |title=Argentina's World Cup ends with punches and in disgrace |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/leandro-paredes-red-card-argentina-spain-world-cup-b3017827.html |access-date=July 20, 2026 |website=The Independent |language=en |archive-date=July 19, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260719230136/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/leandro-paredes-red-card-argentina-spain-world-cup-b3017827.html |url-status=live }}

===Aftermath and reactions===
The Spain national team returned to Madrid the next day and was welcomed at the [[Madrid–Barajas Airport]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Naishadham |first=Suman |date=July 20, 2026 |title=Spain's World Cup champions return home for royal welcome and parade through Madrid |url=https://apnews.com/article/spain-fifa-world-cup-champions-team-cd1705a614f6ffd79da5e217f63faaaa |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260720175301/https://apnews.com/article/spain-fifa-world-cup-champions-team-cd1705a614f6ffd79da5e217f63faaaa |archive-date=July 20, 2026 |access-date=July 20, 2026 |website=[[AP News]] |language=en}}</ref> A World Cup victory parade took place in central Madrid, with roughly two million people in attendance.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dos millones de personas reciben a la selección de España |url=https://www.dw.com/es/dos-millones-de-personas-reciben-a-la-selecci%C3%B3n-de-espa%C3%B1a-en-madrid/a-78042665 |access-date=July 21, 2026 |website=Deutsche Welle |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Gosende |first=Ana |last2=Vicedo |first2=Paula |date=July 20, 2026 |title=Dos millones de personas inundan las calles de Madrid: 'En 2030 la Copa volverá a ser nuestra' |url=https://www.elmundo.es/deportes/2026/07/21/6a5e9d0ae9cf4ac0438b4597.html |access-date=July 21, 2026 |website=El Mundo |language=es|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Celebrations also broke out across various other parts of Spain.<ref>{{Cite news |date=July 19, 2026 |title=Las celebraciones de España tras ganar su segundo Mundial, en imágenes |url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2026-07-20/las-celebraciones-de-espana-tras-ganar-su-segundo-mundial-en-imagenes.html |work=[[El País]] |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lyons |first=Emmet |date=July 20, 2026 |title=Spain rejoices in World Cup victory, even if some fans say Trump lingered too long in team's photo-op |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/spain-world-cup-2026-fans-trump-photo/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260720174342/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/worldcup/2026/07/19/donald-trump-world-cup-trophy-spain-celebrations/90977197007/ |archive-date=July 20, 2026 |access-date=July 20, 2026 |website=[[CBS News]] |language=en-US}}</ref> In [[Ciudad Rodrigo|Ciudad Rodrigo, Salamanca]], several revelers stood in a fountain which collapsed on them, killing a teenager and injuring three others.<ref>{{Cite news |date=July 20, 2026 |title=Muere un adolescente tras el derrumbe de una fuente en Ciudad Rodrigo en las celebraciones del Mundial |url=https://www.elconfidencial.com/espana/castilla-y-leon/2026-07-20/derrumbe-fuente-ciudad-rodrigo-1tna-1tps_4392637/ |work=[[El Confidencial]] |language=es}}</ref> A 20-year-old died in [[Sonseca]] during what was reported as a convulsion. Across Spain that evening, more than 80 people were reported injured and approximately 12 arrested.<ref>{{Cite news |date=July 20, 2026 |title=Celebraciones nocturnas por victoria de España dejan dos muertos y más de 80 heridos |url=https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/07/20/mundial/dos-muertos-y-mas-de-80-heridos-tras-festejos-por-triunfo-de-espana-en-el-mundial |work=[[La Jornada]] |language=es}}</ref> In New York City, celebrations broke out in several parts of the city, including [[Times Square]], [[Central Park]], and [[Little Spain, Manhattan]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Dhaliwal |first=Naveen |last2=Kliger |first2=Hannah |last3=Ramos |first3=Andrew |date=July 19, 2026 |title=Fans who couldn't score tickets to World Cup final in N.J. head to NYC watch parties |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/news/nyc-world-cup-fan-reaction-watch-parties/ |work=[[CBS News]]}}</ref> In [[Mexico City]], several Spain supporters and Mexico national team fans celebrated at the [[Fuente de Cibeles (Mexico City)|Fountain of Cybele]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=George |first=Israel |date=July 29, 2026 |title=Españoles en CdMx celebran triunfo de España en la Copa Mundial 2026 |url=https://www.milenio.com/comunidad/fiesta-en-el-angel-de-la-independencia-por-final-de-mundial-2026 |work=La Afición |publisher=[[Milenio]] |language=Spanish|url-access=limited}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Méndez |first=Arturo |date=July 19, 2026 |title=Festejaron en la capital: Miles de aficionados se reunieron en la Cibeles de la CDMX para celebrar el campeonato del mundo |url=https://oem.com.mx/esto/mundial-2026/aficionados-espanoles-festejaron-en-la-cibeles-de-la-cdmx-31207112 |url-access=limited |work=ESTO |publisher=[[Organización Editorial Mexicana]] |language=es}}</ref>

In [[Buenos Aires]], fans and government officials gathered at [[Ezeiza International Airport]] to receive the Argentina national team, where the [[Armed Forces of the Argentine Republic|Argentine Armed Forces]] performed an orchestra rendition of the [[football chant]] ''{{ill|Muchachos, ahora nos volvimos a ilusionar|lt=|es|Muchachos, ahora nos volvimos a ilusionar}}'' ({{Translation|Guys, we have our hopes up again}}) and a [[Drone art|drone show]] marked their arrival.<ref>{{Cite news |date=20 July 2026 |title=La selección argentina llegó al país tras la final del Mundial: parte del plantel recibió el saludo de una multitud en Ezeiza |url=https://www.a24.com/deportes/la-seleccion-argentina-regresa-al-pais-y-los-hinchas-esperan-al-plantel-el-predio-la-afa-n1577048 |work=[[América 24]] |language=Spanish|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260721134917/https://www.a24.com/deportes/la-seleccion-argentina-regresa-al-pais-y-los-hinchas-esperan-al-plantel-el-predio-la-afa-n1577048|archive-date=21 July 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> Messi and several other players did not travel to Buenos Aires, instead flying directly to their club destinations or to begin their vacations. The arriving players were transported through the city on an open-top bus, greeted by large crowds and fireworks along the route.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Rodríguez |first=Irene |date=21 July 2026 |title=Argentina recibe a la selección con una fiesta tras perder la final del Mundial ante España, sin Leo Messi |url=https://www.antena3.com/noticias/deportes/futbol/argentina-recibe-seleccion-fiesta-obelisco-perder-final-mundial-espana-leo-messi_202607216a5f180e303ca6202cc2ceaf.html |work=Antena 3 |language=Spanish|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260722143444/https://www.antena3.com/noticias/deportes/futbol/argentina-recibe-seleccion-fiesta-obelisco-perder-final-mundial-espana-leo-messi_202607216a5f180e303ca6202cc2ceaf.html|archive-date=22 July 2026|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Preve |first=Clara |last2=Debre |first2=Isabel |date=July 20, 2026 |title=Argentinos salen a las calles para homenajear a selección pese a derrota en final del Mundial |url=https://www.latimes.com/espanol/deportes/articulo/2026-07-20/argentinos-salen-las-calles-para-homenajear-seleccion-pese-derrota-en-final-del-mundial |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |language=Spanish}}</ref> Thousands of additional supporters gathered at the [[Obelisco de Buenos Aires|Obelisk]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=19 July 2026 |title=Miles de hinchas se juntaron en el Obelisco para apoyar a la Selección Argentina tras la final del Mundial |url=https://radiomitre.cienradios.com/deportes/miles-de-hinchas-se-juntaron-en-el-obelisco-para-apoyar-a-la-seleccion-argentina-tras-la-final-del-mundial/ |work=[[Radio Mitre]] |language=Spanish}}</ref> Riots broke out amidst the celebrations, with people throwing stones, glass bottles, and other objects at police.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Fans riot in Argentina after World Cup defeat to Spain|url= https://www.belfastlive.co.uk/news/uk-world-news/fans-riot-argentina-after-world-34317943|work=Belfast Live|date=July 20, 2026|last1=Cailer|first1=Adam|last2=Care|first2=Adam|last3=Davies|first3=Ethan|access-date=July 20, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Argentina fans throw stones at police in Buenos Aires after World Cup final loss|url=https://www.channelnewsasia.com/shorts/argentina-fans-throw-stones-police-in-buenos-aires-after-world-cup-final-loss-6265211|work=Channel News Asia|access-date=July 20, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Argentina fans hurl rocks at riot police after World Cup defeat|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/world-news/2026/07/20/argentina-fans-throw-rocks-police-world-cup-buenos-aires/|work=The Daily Telegraph|date=July 20, 2026|last=Smith|first=Emily|access-date=July 20, 2026}}</ref> Riot police responded with water cannons, tear gas, and rubber bullets to disperse the crowds. Local police reported at least fifteen arrests and several injuries during the clashes.<ref>{{Cite news|date=July 20, 2026|title=Without Messi, Argentine team set for low-key homecoming|url=https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260720-without-messi-argentine-team-set-for-low-key-homecoming|work=France24|access-date=July 20, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=July 20, 2026|title=Argentina fans clash with police in Buenos Aires after World Cup final defeat|url=https://www.tbsnews.net/world/argentina-fans-clash-police-buenos-aires-after-world-cup-final-defeat-1492921|work=[[The Business Standard]]|access-date=July 21, 2026}}</ref>

On July 29, [[FIFA]] opened formal disciplinary proceedings against the [[Argentine Football Association]] (AFA), citing multiple infractions by the Argentina national team during the final and their semi-final match against [[England national football team|England]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Botcherby |first=Elizabeth |date=29 July 2026 |title=Fifa opens disciplinary proceedings against Argentina |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cp3rkwgy6y7o |work=[[BBC Sport]]}}</ref> On August 21, FIFA's disciplinary committee announced a 10-match ban for [[Leandro Paredes]], a 7-match ban for [[Nahuel Molina]], a 3-match ban for [[Roberto Ayala]], and a 1-match ban for both [[Thiago Almada]] and Spain's [[Gavi (footballer)|Gavi]], in addition to financial sanctions for all of them, with fines totaling $270,000. The committee fined the AFA $321,000 ($100,000 of which is suspended) for displaying a banner with the words "Las Malvinas son Argentinas" ("[[Falkland Islands|The Falklands]] are Argentine") during the semi-final, in reference to the territory [[Falkland Islands sovereignty dispute|dispute between Argentina and the United Kingdom]]. FIFA also sanctioned the AFA with a maximum 50% capacity for its next two home matches.<ref>{{cite web |last=Brotherton |first=Alex |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c98v7p1pr3eo |title=Argentina's Paredes banned for 10 games |publisher=BBC Sport |date=21 August 2026 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sanz |first=Miguel Ángel |date=2026-08-21 |title=Duras sanciones tras la pelea de la vergüenza |url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/mundial/2026/08/21/duras-saciones-pelea-vergueenza.html |access-date=2026-08-21 |website=MARCA |language=es}}</ref>

==Entertainment==

===Closing ceremony===
[[File:FIFAAH-06520 President Donald J. Trump and First Lady Melania Trump attend the FIFA World Cup Final.jpg|thumb|upright=1.10|Smoke in the national colors of Spain and Argentina drifts across MetLife Stadium's pitch minutes before kickoff.|210x210px]]

A closing ceremony for the World Cup began at 1:40&nbsp;p.m. [[Eastern Time Zone|Eastern Daylight Time]] ([[UTC−4]]), eighty minutes before the scheduled kickoff. [[IShowSpeed]] performed his World Cup-themed song "[[World Cup (Champions)|Champions]]", while headliner [[Post Malone]] and rapper [[Swae Lee]] sang "[[Sunflower (Post Malone and Swae Lee song)|Sunflower]]". Robbie Williams, [[Nicole Scherzinger]] and [[Laura Pausini]] performed the song "Desire". [[Jennifer Hudson]] sang the [[The Star-Spangled Banner|U.S. national anthem]], [[María Becerra]] sang [[Argentine National Anthem|Argentina's national anthem]], and the Spanish brass quintet {{ill|Spanish Brass|es}} performed [[Marcha Real|Spain's national anthem]]. [[Mario Kempes]] and [[Andrés Iniesta]], two respective members of Argentina's and Spain's winning teams in 1978 and 2010, unveiled the [[FIFA World Cup Trophy]].{{efn|Attributed to multiple references:<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Chan |first=Anna |date=July 14, 2026 |title=World Cup Closing Ceremony to Feature Jennifer Hudson, Nicole Scherzinger & More |url=https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/world-cup-closing-ceremony-jennifer-hudson-nicole-scherzinger-1236293796/ |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |access-date=July 14, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260715064512/https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/world-cup-closing-ceremony-jennifer-hudson-nicole-scherzinger-1236293796/ |archive-date=July 15, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=July 19, 2026 |title=History made by stunning closing ceremony and Halftime Show |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/best-of-closing-ceremony-halftime-show |access-date=July 24, 2026 |website=FIFA|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260719225809/https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/best-of-closing-ceremony-halftime-show|archive-date=July 19, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Who's singing Argentina's national anthem before the 2026 World Cup Final vs. Spain today? |url=https://bolavip.com/en/world-cup/whos-singing-argentinas-national-anthem-before-the-2026-world-cup-final-vs-spain |access-date=July 20, 2026 |agency= |date=July 19, 2026 |archive-date=July 19, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260719190159/https://bolavip.com/en/world-cup/whos-singing-argentinas-national-anthem-before-the-2026-world-cup-final-vs-spain |url-status=live |last=Pinheiro|first=Ariadna|work=Bolavip USA}}</ref>}}
===Halftime show===
{{main|2026 FIFA World Cup final halftime show}}
[[File:P20260719DT-1237 President Donald J. Trump and First Lady Melania Trump attend the FIFA World Cup Final.jpg|thumb|[[Shakira]] and the [[Ghetto Kids]] performing "[[Dai Dai]]" during the [[2026 FIFA World Cup final halftime show|halftime show]]]]
The 2026 final was the first final in World Cup history to include a [[halftime show]], similar to the halftime shows featured at the NFL [[Super Bowl]]. It was co-headlined by singer-songwriters [[Madonna]] and [[Shakira]], South Korean boy band [[BTS]], and [[Justin Bieber]], and featured guest performances from [[Burna Boy]] and [[Emmanuel Kelly]]. [[Jason Sudeikis]] and [[Brendan Hunt]] appeared as the characters [[Ted Lasso (character)|Ted Lasso]] and [[Coach Beard]], respectively, from the television series ''[[Ted Lasso]].'' Other performers included the rock group [[Dr. Teeth and the Electric Mayhem|Electric Mayhem]] from [[The Muppets]], the [[Ghetto Kids]], the [[PS22 Chorus]], and a combined [[New York Philharmonic]] and [[Simón Bolívar Symphony Orchestra]], with [[Bijan Mortazavi]] and conducted by [[Gustavo Dudamel]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Hustin |first=Caitlin |title=Madonna, Justin Bieber, BTS, Shakira Headline Jam-Packed First-Ever FIFA World Cup Final Halftime Show |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/music/music-news/fifa-world-cup-halftime-madonna-justin-bieber-bts-shakira-1236651689/ |magazine=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=July 19, 2026 |access-date=July 19, 2026 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260719204241/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/music/music-news/fifa-world-cup-halftime-madonna-justin-bieber-bts-shakira-1236651689/ |archive-date=July 19, 2026 }}</ref> The show was part of an effort to reach $100 million for the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund, which seeks to increase access to education and sports for children.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 14, 2026 |title=Madonna, Shakira, and BTS to Co-Headline the First-Ever FIFA World Cup™ Final Halftime Show |url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260514891433/en/Madonna-Shakira-and-BTS-to-Co-Headline-the-First-Ever-FIFA-World-Cup-Final-Halftime-Show |access-date=August 1, 2026 |website=[[Business Wire]]}}</ref> 

The halftime show was criticized by some commentators and fans as being too commercialized and an unwanted Americanization of the match.<ref>{{cite news |last=Church |first=Ben |date=May 15, 2026 |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2026/05/15/sport/world-cup-halftime-show-reaction |title=Why some purists can't stand the idea of a World Cup halftime show |publisher=CNN |access-date=June 26, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260516130825/https://edition.cnn.com/2026/05/15/sport/world-cup-halftime-show-reaction |archive-date=May 16, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Guardian-Halftime">{{cite news |last=Hughes |first=Matt |date=June 10, 2026 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/10/tv-rights-holders-frustrated-over-world-cup-final-half-time-show-delay |title=TV rights holders frustrated over World Cup final half-time show delay |work=The Guardian |access-date=June 26, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260610181725/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/10/tv-rights-holders-frustrated-over-world-cup-final-half-time-show-delay |archive-date=June 10, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> The halftime break lasted 27 minutes and 22 seconds,<ref>{{cite news |last=Halpert |first=Madeline |date=July 19, 2026 |title=Shakira, Madonna, Justin Bieber and BTS perform at colourful World Cup half-time show |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/clyxjl0wkl7o |access-date=July 24, 2026 |publisher=[[BBC]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260721021010/https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/clyxjl0wkl7o |archive-date=July 21, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> which broke the [[Laws of the Game (association football)|IFAB Laws of the Game]] which state that the halftime break cannot exceed 15 minutes.{{efn|Attributed to multiple references:<ref name="Guardian-Halftime"/><ref>{{cite news |last1=Sheldon |first1=Dan |last2=Crafton |first2=Adam |date=July 14, 2026 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7445380/2026/07/14/world-cup-half-time-length-fifa/ |title=FIFA targeting 20-minute break for World Cup half-time |access-date=July 15, 2026 |work=The Athletic |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260714194433/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7445380/2026/07/14/world-cup-half-time-length-fifa/ |archive-date=July 14, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Marcotti |first=Gabriele |author-link=Gabriele Marcotti |date=March 8, 2025 |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/44164198/fifa-world-cup-half-show-gianni-infantino-only-15-minutes-super-bowl |title=FIFA can have a World Cup halftime show... within 15 minutes |access-date=June 26, 2026 |publisher=ESPN |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260514115407/https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/44164198/fifa-world-cup-half-show-gianni-infantino-only-15-minutes-super-bowl |archive-date=May 14, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>}}
